{{Short description|German mathematician and astronomer}}
[[File:RLHannover.jpg|thumb|150px|Raphael Levi Hannover]]
'''Raphael Levi Hannover''' (1685 – May 17, 1779) was a German [[Jews|Jewish]] [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]].  The son of Jacob Joseph, Hannover was born at [[Weikersheim]], [[Franconia]] in 1685. He was educated at the [[Jewish]] school of Hanover and at the yeshivah of [[Frankfurt am Main]], and became bookkeeper in the firm of [[Simon Wolf Oppenheimer]] in [[Hanover]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Schulze |first=Peter |chapter=Levi, Rafael |title=Hannoversches Biographisches Lexikon: Von den Anfängen bis in die Gegenwart |editor-first=Dirk |editor-last=Böttcher |publisher=Schlütersche |date=2002 |page=291 |isbn=3-87706-706-9 |language=de}}</ref> Here he attracted the attention of [[Gottfried Leibniz|Leibniz]], and for a number of years was one of his most distinguished pupils and lived by him for three years (including last secretary),<ref name=Benbassa>{{cite book |author=Benbassa, Esther|authorlink1=Esther Benbassa |author2= Attias, Jean-Christophe |author3= Gisel, Pierre |title=Europe et les juifs |publisher= Labor et Fides |date=2002 |isbn= 978-2-8309-1048-3 |page=120 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r9iR_dJE4tgC|language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Schulte |first=Christoph |chapter=Leibniz und sein ‘Schüler’ Raphael Levi |title=Leibniz und das Judentum |editor-first=Hartmut |editor-last=Rudolph |location=Stuttgart |publisher=Franz Steiner |date=2008 |isbn=978-3-515-09251-7 |pages=35–48 |language=de}}</ref> and afterward teacher of mathematics, astronomy, and natural philosophy. He also corresponded with [[Moses Mendelssohn]].<ref name=Benbassa/>

Raphael Levi Hannover wrote: "Luḥot ha-'Ibbur," astronomical tables for the [[Jewish calendar]];<ref>Leyden-Hanover, 1756</ref> "Tekunat ha-Shamayim," on astronomy and calendar-making, especially commenting on the [[Talmudical]] passages on these topics, with glosses of Moses Tiktin.<ref>Amsterdam, 1756</ref> An enlarged revision of the latter work, with two other astronomical works of his, is in manuscript. The "Luḥot ha-'Ibbur" has been published with [[Meyer Fürth|M. E. Fürth]]'s "Yir'at Shamayim," on Maimonides' "Yad," Ḳiddush ha-Ḥodesh.<ref>Dessau, 1820-21</ref> He died in [[Hanover]] in 1779.
